title: Skin depth of copper at 1 MHz
caption: A high-frequency field enters a conductor only a short way: its amplitude falls as e^{−z/δ} with δ = √(2/(μ₀σω)) = 65.0 μm ≈ 65 μm for copper (σ = 6 × 10⁷ S m⁻¹) at 1 MHz. At one skin depth 37% of the surface amplitude remains; at 3δ (195 μm) only 5.0%. The current flows in a thin skin, so a hollow or plated conductor carries RF as well as a solid one.
alt: Graph of field amplitude against depth into copper: an exponential decay from 1 at the surface, 0.37 at 65 μm and 0.05 at 195 μm.
description: The horizontal axis is the depth into the copper in micrometres; the vertical axis is the field amplitude as a fraction of the surface value.
The amplitude falls as e^{−z/δ} with δ = 65 μm.
At z = δ = 65 μm it is 0.37; at z = 3δ = 195 μm it is 0.05.
